data.hook: Researchers tested top AI models with identical conflict stories, swapping only the gender of the person at fault. The results showed a clear pattern: men faced blame and punishment, while women got empathy.
data.name: Study Reveals AI Judges Men Harsher Than Women in Same Scenarios
data.summary: A new preprint paper from Chinese researchers introduced GAMA-Bench, with 1,298 matched scenarios in relationships and social conflicts. Ten leading large language models consistently used more punitive words for male actors—about 3.3 extra per response—along with higher blame and escalation, while female actors received 1.3 more therapeutic words and greater empathy. This held across models, even with step-by-step reasoning. Commenters linked it to biases in human training data, raising concerns about AI in real decisions.

data.summary: Tencent released Hy4-Flash around November 16, 2026, an open-weight model with 224 billion parameters that activates just 12 billion per token via Mixture-of-Experts design. Meanwhile, between November 8 and 10, attackers at Prime Intellect swapped DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with an uncensored version for 53 hours, dodging refusals but sparking worries over model verification in shared services. Developers praise its productivity edge, like 1/20th the cost of bigger models on office tasks, as the community tests it for research and workflows.

data.summary: From November 8 at 01:24 UTC to November 10 at 06:35 UTC, Prime Intellect's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash endpoint served a modified 'abliterated' model that refused just 1% of safety prompts, compared to 83-98% for the original. The incident highlights supply chain vulnerabilities in AI, with calls for model verification like cryptographic signing to ensure users query the right weights.

data.hook: MIT researchers reveal how smart harness designs turn language models into compositional powerhouses, tackling tasks far beyond their training data.
data.name: MIT Paper Shows Language Model Harnesses Boost Generalization
data.summary: A new MIT CSAIL paper by Alex L. Zhang, Souradip Chakraborty, and Omar Khattab argues that well-designed harnesses enable models to compose capabilities for stronger generalization on long or new tasks. By keeping prompts locally in-distribution through abstractions like context offloading and recursive sub-agent calls, these harnesses avoid errors from growing context windows in standard agents. Experiments on benchmarks like OOLONG and OBLiQ-Bench demonstrate models generalizing to tasks 8–64× longer, with gains like a 27B-parameter model improving 27% on long-context suites using fewer tokens. Co-authors stress that harness design and model learning are deeply intertwined, countering views that stronger models will make them obsolete.

data.name: TensorLean Verifies AI GPU Kernels and Uncovers Hidden Bugs
data.summary: Researchers from CertiK and Columbia University launched TensorLean, a framework that formally verifies production GPU kernels for large AI models. It checked 149 instances, proving 83 correct and finding 38 bugs missed by standard testing—including 23 in FlashAttention and 2 in DeepSeek’s DeepGEMM. The bugs involved memory errors, numerical issues, and faulty algorithms, with all reported to maintainers. This machine-checkable approach offers stronger guarantees than tests by covering all valid inputs, helping AI teams ensure optimizations don't break results.

data.name: MIT Study Reveals AI Coding Boosts Output but Not Finished Software
data.summary: The study by Mert Demirer, Leon Musolff, and Liyuan Yang examined over 500,000 GitHub developers and found AI autocomplete raised coding activity by 30%, interactive agents by 180%, and autonomous agents by 240%. Yet releases increased only 30%, new apps across stores roughly doubled, and overall user engagement stayed flat. Human bottlenecks in review, testing, deployment, and building audiences persist, with abandoned repos rising from 60% to 69% after tool adoption. Observers note the shift from code-writing ease to the harder work of curation, quality, and finding users who return.
